title: Detected command is a CPU feature probe, not a usable CLI
reasoning: The top-level main does not implement a command interface: it treats argv[argc-1] as a float buffer and feeds it to AVX/FMA intrinsics. If this semantic feature is surfaced as a runnable cpu_fma3 CLI command, normal invocation can execute undefined behavior or crash because argv points to command-line strings, not a guaranteed 32-byte float array. The file appears to be a compile/runtime CPU capability check rather than an application entrypoint.
recommendation: Exclude NumPy distutils CPU check sources under vendored python-runtime/site-packages from CLI-command feature extraction, or classify this as a build probe/internal check instead of a user-facing command.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for the feature extraction classification, and the file itself contains only the probe main.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a feature-detection regression test asserting numpy/distutils/checks/cpu_*.c files in vendored python-runtime are not emitted as cli-command features.
minimumFixScope: Update the semantic feature extractor or its ignore rules for vendored NumPy CPU check files.

history.note: Excluded vendored frontend/python-runtime dependency probe from WindieOS-owned review scope
